proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOE's Office of Nuclear Energy substantially limit its size and scope, start no new civilian reactor demonstration or commercialization projects, and leave licensing support and commercialization to the private sector. It would refocus on basic research, three lines of work (fuels, reactor technology, waste) and a leaner budget.

status_summary: The government expanded DOE's role in reactor testing and demonstration rather than limiting it. Executive Order 14301 (signed 2025-05-23) directed DOE to create a Reactor Pilot Program with a goal of at least three reactors reaching criticality by 2026-07-04; Nuclear News reported on 2026-07-02 that three companies had done so, and DOE's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad, reported 2026-03-09, extends the pilot programs. DOE announced conditional HALEU fuel allocations on 2025-08-26, including for a pilot program reactor. The Office of Nuclear Energy continues and moved under the Under Secretary for Energy in the 2025-11-20 reorganization. Congress's FY2026 appropriation (Public Law 119-74, 2026-01-23) provided 1.685 billion dollars for Nuclear Energy, above the 1.37 billion requested, and transferred 3.1 billion dollars of infrastructure law funds for up to two advanced small modular reactors, per CRS.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14301 signed, directing DOE to create a Reactor Pilot Program (published 2025-05-29).
DOE announced a second round of conditional HALEU allocations to three companies, including fuel for a pilot program reactor.
DOE reorganization chart moved the Office of Nuclear Energy under the Under Secretary for Energy; the office remains.

FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations enacted (P.L. 119-74); per CRS, Nuclear Energy received 1.685 billion dollars and 3.1 billion dollars of infrastructure law funds were transferred for small modular reactor demonstrations.
DOE announced the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad extending and expanding the reactor and fuel line pilot programs.
Nuclear News reported three pilot program reactors had reached DOE-authorized criticality, meeting the 2026-07-04 goal.

title: Limit DOE Nuclear Energy scope and start no new reactor demonstrations
uncertainties: The pilot reactors are developed by private companies under DOE authorization; whether this counts as DOE initiating demonstration projects is a matter of reading. The ANS reorganization article is trade press. The FY2027 Nuclear Energy request was not checked.
